title: Arbitration v Conciliation v Mediation
lead: One comparison chart across ==thirteen dimensions== — governing law, initiation, procedure, outcome, enforceability, cost, appeal and flexibility. The single most examinable table in the ADR block.

head: Aspect
Arbitration
Conciliation
Mediation
rows: ==Mediation Act, 2023==; CPC s.89; SC Mediation Rules
==Written arbitration agreement or clause==; notice of arbitration
Mutual consent; ==written invitation to conciliate==; appointment of conciliator
Mutual consent; ==court referral==; pre-litigation mediation under the 2023 Act
==Arbitrator(s)== appointed by parties or court — impartial and independent
==Mediator== chosen by parties or appointed — must be ==certified== under the 2023 Act
Less formal; joint and separate meetings; ==may suggest settlement terms==
Informal; ==facilitates dialogue==; joint and private sessions; ==no power to impose==
==Binding arbitral award== — final, enforceable like a court decree
==Non-binding settlement==, binding once signed by parties
==Non-binding mediated settlement==, made binding by court order
Under ==s.28== of the Mediation Act; ==challengeable within 90 days==
Confidential proceedings; ==award may be public== unless agreed otherwise
==All civil, commercial, family==; exceptions in the First Schedule
Limited to appointment, interim measures, enforcement/setting aside
==Minimal== — court may appoint if parties fail to agree
==Generally higher== — arbitrator fees, venue, legal representation
==Usually lowest== — mediator fees, possible enforcement court fees
==No appeal== — treated as an arbitral award
Limited challenge under ==s.29== of the Mediation Act
==Adjudicatory== — binding decision on evidence and law
==Facilitative== — helps parties find their own solution
Less flexible — agreed or institutional rules
==Highly flexible== — parties control process and outcome
